**System name:** Alpha Centauri (α Centauri, α Cen), a triple star system in the constellation Centaurus. Its components are:
- Alpha Centauri A (Rigil Kentaurus)
- Alpha Centauri B (Toliman)
- Alpha Centauri C (Proxima Centauri)

The system as a whole has two confirmed planets, both around Proxima Centauri.

**Planets of Proxima Centauri (Alpha Centauri C)**
- **Proxima b (Alpha Centauri Cb): confirmed.**
  - Terrestrial planet discovered in 2016 by ESO.
  - Minimum mass about 1.17 Earth masses.
  - Orbits at about 0.049 AU, in the habitable zone (though unlikely to be habitable).
- **Proxima d: confirmed.**
  - Detected in 2022 and confirmed in 2025.
  - Sub-Earth of about 0.29 Earth masses.
  - Orbital period about 5.15 days, very close to the star.
- **Proxima c: disputed, with inconclusive evidence.**
  - Formally published in 2020 as a super-Earth or mini-Neptune.
  - Mass about 7 Earth masses, orbit about 1.49 AU, period 1,928 days (5.28 years).
  - A 2022 study disputed its existence.
  - As of 2025, NIRPS spectrograph observations could not confirm it, but found hints of a lower-amplitude signal with a similar period.

**Planets of Alpha Centauri A**
- **Alpha Centauri Ab (Candidate 1 / C1): unconfirmed.**
  - First detected in 2021 as a candidate at about 1.1 AU, which may be a dust disk or an artefact. The possibility of a background star has been ruled out.
  - JWST observations in August 2024 found a point source at about 2 AU, believed to be the same object. It is not a background object and is unlikely to be an instrumental artifact.
  - It was not recovered and needs more observations. There is a 52% chance it was not re-observed because of orbital motion.
  - If it is a planet, it would have a mass of 90–150 Earth masses (Saturn-mass), a radius of 1.0–1.1 Jupiter radii and a temperature of about 225 K.
  - Orbital period 2–3 years, eccentricity about 0.4.

**Planets of Alpha Centauri B**
- **Alpha Centauri Bb: disproven.**
  - Claimed in 2012 as an Earth-mass planet with a 3.2-day orbit.
  - Shown in 2015 to be an artefact of radial-velocity data processing.
- **"Alpha Centauri Bc": not a claimed discovery.**
  - Hubble searched for transits in 2013–2014 and detected one possible transit-like event. It could be a planet of about 0.92 Earth radii with an orbital period of 20.4 days or less.
  - The name has not been used in the literature.

Toliman has no known planets.

**Other:** Hypothetical additional planets may exist, but no observational studies have found brown dwarfs or gas giants apart from the possible Ab. A possible sparse circumstellar disc around α Cen AB was suggested from infrared excess.

  - Proxima Centauri (α Cen C), an M-class red dwarf.
- **Proxima Centauri** is the closest star to the Sun, at 4.2465 ly (1.3020 pc).
- **α Cen AB** is the nearest binary system, at 4.344 ly (1.33 pc). A and B are the nearest stars visible to the naked eye.
- Proxima lies about 13,000 AU (0.21 ly) from α Cen AB. Radial velocity measurements in 2017 showed it is gravitationally bound to AB, with an orbital period of about 511,000 years.

## Planets

**Proxima Centauri (two confirmed planets)**
- **Proxima b** (Alpha Centauri Cb):
  - Terrestrial planet discovered in 2016 by ESO astronomers.
  - Minimum mass about 1.17 Earth masses.
  - Orbits at about 0.049 AU, in the habitable zone, though it is unlikely to be habitable.
- **Proxima d**:
  - Sub-Earth with a mass of about 0.29 Earth masses.
  - Orbital period of about 5.15 days, very close to the star.
  - Detected as a candidate in 2022 and confirmed in 2025 (NIRPS).
- **Proxima c** (disputed candidate):
  - Possible mini-Neptune or super-Earth, with a mass of about 7 Earth masses.
  - Orbits at about 1.49 AU with a period of 1,928 days (5.28 yr).
  - Formally published in 2020. A 2022 study disputed its existence.
  - As of 2025, evidence remains inconclusive. NIRPS could not confirm it but found hints of a lower-amplitude signal with a similar period.

**Alpha Centauri A**
- **Alpha Centauri Ab / Candidate 1 (C1)** is unconfirmed.
  - First detected in 2021, at about 1.1 AU with a period of about one year. It could be a dust disk or an artefact.
  - JWST observations in August 2024 found a point source at about 2 AU, believed to be the same object. It is not a background object and is unlikely to be an instrumental artifact.
  - If it is a planet, it would have 90–150 Earth masses, a radius of 1.0–1.1 RJ, and a temperature of about 225 K, with an orbital period of 2–3 years.
  - It was not re-observed, so it needs more observations to be confirmed.

**Alpha Centauri B**
- **Alpha Centauri Bb**, an Earth-mass planet in a 3.2-day orbit claimed in 2012, was disproven in 2015 as an artefact of data processing.
- A possible transit-like event seen by Hubble (2013–14) could indicate a planet of about 0.92 Earth radii with an orbital period of 20.4 days or less. It would be called "Bc" if confirmed, but it is not a claimed discovery.

**Summary:** The system as a whole has two confirmed planets, Proxima b and Proxima d. Proxima c and Alpha Centauri Ab remain disputed or unconfirmed candidates. Toliman (α Cen B) has no known planets.

outcome:
**Closest star system to the Solar System: Alpha Centauri**, a triple star system in the constellation Centaurus.
- Its stars are Alpha Centauri A (Rigil Kentaurus), Alpha Centauri B (Toliman) and Alpha Centauri C (Proxima Centauri).
- Proxima Centauri is the closest single star to the Sun, at about 4.2465 ly (1.302 pc).
- Alpha Centauri AB is the nearest binary, at about 4.344 ly. A and B are the nearest stars visible to the naked eye.
- Proxima lies about 13,000 AU (0.21 ly) from AB, and radial velocity measurements in 2017 showed it is gravitationally bound to AB.

**Planets around Proxima Centauri (Alpha Centauri C)**
- **Proxima b (Alpha Centauri Cb)**: confirmed.
  - It is a terrestrial planet discovered in 2016 by ESO astronomers.
  - Its minimum mass is about 1.17 Earth masses.
  - It orbits about 0.049 AU from the star, in the habitable zone, though it is unlikely to be habitable.
- **Proxima d**: confirmed.
  - It is a sub-Earth of about 0.29 Earth masses, with a 5.15-day orbit very close to the star.
  - It was detected as a candidate in 2022 and confirmed in 2025 (NIRPS).
- **Proxima c**: disputed, possibly a mini-Neptune or super-Earth.
  - Its mass is about 7 Earth masses and its orbit is about 1.49 AU, with a period of 1,928 days (5.28 yr).
  - Its discovery was formally published in 2020, and a possible direct-imaging detection in June 2020 hinted at a large ring system.
  - A 2022 study disputed its existence.
  - As of 2025 the evidence is inconclusive. NIRPS could not confirm it, but found hints of a lower-amplitude signal with a similar period.

**Planets around Alpha Centauri A (unconfirmed)**
- **Alpha Centauri Ab / "Candidate 1" (C1)**:
  - It was first detected in 2021 at about 1.1 AU, with a period of about 1 year.
  - JWST observations in August 2024 found a point source at about 2 AU, believed to be the same object. It is not a background object and is unlikely to be an instrumental artifact.
  - It was not recovered and needs more observations, so it is not confirmed.
  - If real, it would be a Saturn-mass giant planet with 90–150 Earth masses, a radius of 1.0–1.1 Jupiter radii, a temperature of about 225 K, an orbital period of 2–3 years and an eccentricity of about 0.4.

**Planets around Alpha Centauri B**
- **Alpha Centauri Bb**: an Earth-mass planet with a 3.2-day orbit, claimed in 2012. It was refuted in 2015 as an artefact of data processing.
- **Possible "Alpha Centauri Bc"**: a Hubble search in 2013–2014 found one transit-like event.
  - The possible planet would have a radius of about 0.92 Earth radii and an orbital period of 20.4 days or less.
  - It is not a claimed discovery, and the name has not been used in the literature.

**Summary:** The Alpha Centauri system has two confirmed planets, Proxima b and Proxima d. Proxima c is disputed, Alpha Centauri Ab is a candidate, and Toliman (B) has no known planets.
